questions.text: How would you describe the discharge — colour, consistency, and when during urination or at other times does it appear?
questions.purpose: Characterise discharge to differentiate gonorrhoea (purulent yellow-green) from non-gonococcal urethritis (clear or white)
options: Clear or white, watery — occurs mostly in the morning
Clear or white, mucoid — occurs throughout the day
Only visible when urethra is squeezed

questions.text: Have you had unprotected sexual contact with a new partner or a partner with a known STI in the past 3 months?
questions.purpose: STI exposure history is the key risk factor for urethral discharge from gonorrhoea or chlamydia

questions.text: Do you have burning or pain when you urinate (dysuria)?
questions.purpose: Dysuria alongside discharge strongly suggests urethritis (gonococcal or non-gonococcal)

questions.text: Have you developed any genital sores, ulcers, or rash alongside the discharge?
questions.purpose: Co-existing ulcers or rash suggest a concurrent STI (syphilis, herpes) requiring broader STI workup

questions.text: Do you have testicular or pelvic pain, or any swelling in the scrotum?
questions.purpose: Testicular pain with discharge may indicate epididymo-orchitis, a complication of ascending STI

questions.text: Have you had any similar episodes before, and have you previously been treated for an STI?
questions.purpose: Recurrent episodes or prior STI history indicates ongoing risk behaviour and need for comprehensive STI screen
